inspiration: Hue ramps for whole-sprite recolour: one greyscale-style source sprite is tinted by a fixed-length ramp indexed by one channel of each pixel, so one body can take many dye looks. Shape to keep for gear dressing (row 15) and per-zone colour grade (row 16). Reference: include/uo/hues.h line 17; src/render/Renderer.cpp line 65.

Target highlight as a single tint on every layer of the targeted mobile, so body and gear highlight together. Reference: src/render/Renderer.cpp line 22. For Frankendom, use a rim or outline and a pulse instead of a flat tint so the target reads at 375 wide without looking dyed.

Light sources are cut when a roof or interior blocks them: an occlusion test checks tiles above the light and suppresses indoor and window lights from outside. Reference: src/render/Renderer.cpp lines 258-274. Idea for torches and zone ambience lights (vfx, camera).

Walk glide: the mobile body animation runs in step with a sub-cell slide, and the local avatar stays centred while the world scrolls under it. Reference: README.md line 356 (renderer section). Idea for hero movement (row 6) so motion reads smooth at phone frame rates.

Painter's-order draw: statics, dynamic items and mobiles are interleaved by height, so a same-height mobile draws over floor items. Equipment is drawn over the body at the same action and frame. Reference: README.md lines 354-356; src/render/Renderer.cpp around line 399. Idea for gear layering (row 15).

Sloped ground: flat tiles are plain blits, while sloped tiles are stretched across four corner heights using a separate texture source. Reference: src/render/Renderer.cpp lines 61-64 (quad flag and source). Idea for terrain look without a new art file per slope.

briefs.label: Dye-ramp body set
briefs.why: A single body silhouette reads as many factions or rarity tiers at 375 wide because only the tint changes. Cheap to ship and easy to read in a crowd.
briefs.keep: One greyscale body with a ramp lookup per dye; the ramp is indexed by one channel, not by hand-painted variants.
briefs.change: Use a shader palette per rarity tier instead of a fixed hue table; add a second accent ring on rare dyes so colour is never the only cue (colour-blind safe). Keep Dom's rule: recreate as a distinct original, never a copy of the donor's palette.
briefs.ref: include/uo/hues.h line 17; src/render/Renderer.cpp line 65 (paths in the donor, not copied)

briefs.label: Target rim pulse
briefs.why: The targeted enemy must be identifiable among up to three attackers (MAX_ATTACKERS = 3). A whole-silhouette cue beats a small icon.
briefs.keep: One cue applied to every layer of the target so the whole silhouette changes together.
briefs.change: Use an outline rim plus a slow pulse, not a flat hue; pick a colour that never matches blood or the hit flash. Keep Dom's rule: an original cue, not the donor's colour.

briefs.label: Roof-cut torch
briefs.why: Indoor light stays indoors. Players read a room as a room without a separate fog layer.
briefs.keep: Lights are suppressed by occlusion above them and by walls for interior and window cases.
briefs.change: Drive the test from zone data (an interior flag per zone) rather than tile heights, so it stays cheap at the 375 px target.

briefs.label: Centred glide walk
briefs.why: A centred avatar with a sliding world keeps the fight camera steady during movement (row 11).
briefs.keep: The avatar stays centred; the world moves under it; the slide is tied to the walk cycle so feet and ground agree.
briefs.change: Use a fixed stride and an ease curve for our hero, not the donor's per-direction timing table. Keep Dom's rule: recreate our own timing from our animations.
